reason: The source diff replaces SearchSpace's promising-activity hash set and global flag with a fixed DynamicBitset. This changes a repeatedly queried search-state representation and the indexing of clients and shipments, making it a solver mechanism with measurable work and semantic risks.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: Bit-indexed promising-activity checks may reduce hash work during local search, permitting more iterations within fixed budgets; incorrect client or shipment indexing could suppress useful moves or corrupt search state.
causal_chain: Search operators repeatedly mark and query promising activities. The PR maps clients from the front and shipments from the back of a fixed bitset, replacing set insertion and membership plus a global all-promising flag. This can change per-move cost and, if the mapping is wrong, the neighbourhood explored.
structural_trigger: Local-search runs that mark and query client activities; shipment-rich instances additionally exercise the reversed shipment index and all-promising transitions.
activation_probe: Count isPromising and markPromising calls in pinned base and PR builds on public CVRP cases, and exercise client, shipment, mark-all, and unmark-all state transitions with targeted upstream tests.
instance_selection_rule: Freeze the existing PyVRP CVRP development, hidden ID, and generated-shift panels before hidden scoring, using one previously fixed private seed for baseline qualification and the full declared seed-budget grid for final Agent judging.
workload_exposure_plan: Run source-only paired builds through the shared PyVRP CVRP driver, trace SearchSpace activity checks on a public instance, and keep a separate shipment-state regression probe because CVRP workloads may not cover the reversed index branch.
mathematical_risk: An off-by-one or aliasing error in bit positions can mark the wrong activity, skip feasible improvements, or pass stale search state into route construction; allocation and bitset size can also fail on larger instances.
independent_check_plan: Verify visit coverage, capacity, and objective on original CVRP instances for every returned route; compare promising-state transitions against a simple reference set for both clients and shipments.
hidden_generalization_plan: Report verified fixed-budget gap trajectories, per-instance regressions, missing runs, and peak memory separately on hidden ID and generated-shift CVRP panels. Human PR benefit requires a separate paired confirmation.
overlap_review: The bitset representation is distinct from PR #1156's route perturbation and PR #1164's operator cache, but their search-state call paths must be compared before multiple tasks are counted.
resource_risk: A fixed bitset can allocate for every activity even when few are promising; benefits may be offset by initialization or cache costs on small instances.
